title: Throttle async calls with leading and trailing runs
prompt: Implement throttleAsync in src/throttle-async.js as `throttleAsync(fn, intervalMs, options)`. It returns a throttled function that invokes `fn` immediately on the first call of a window, opens a window timer for `intervalMs` using `options.clock` (default clock: `{ setTimeout(callback, ms), clearTimeout(handle) }` backed by the global timers), and, when that timer fires, invokes `fn` once more with the newest arguments supplied during the window if there were any. No extra timer may be scheduled while a window is open, and calls arriving during an open window must not invoke `fn` immediately. Every call returns a promise: calls that cause an invocation resolve or reject with that invocation's outcome, and all calls waiting for the trailing invocation share its outcome. After the timer fires the window closes, so the next call opens a new window and invokes `fn` immediately. `throttled.cancel()` clears an open window and rejects the promises waiting for the trailing invocation with an error whose `name` is 'AbortError'; it does nothing when no window is open and must not affect a leading invocation that already started. Throw TypeError for a non-function `fn`, an `intervalMs` that is not a positive finite number, or a clock without callable setTimeout and clearTimeout. Keep the existing named export.
